messages:
Sam R: Hi all — just hit my first payroll and noticed health insurance premium coming out but my HSA contribution didn’t start. I enrolled during onboarding and selected $150/paycheck. Is there a lag?

Talia (People Ops): Welcome Sam! Congrats on joining :tada: There can be a one-pay-period lag depending on when your enrollment was processed. When did you enroll?

Sam R: Enrolled on my first day, 8:30am PT, via the benefits portal. It showed as confirmed.

Miguel (Payroll): Hey Sam — thanks for flagging. If enrollment confirmed after payroll cutoff for that pay period, HSA deductions start next cycle. Can you DM me the enrollment confirmation number? I can check cutoff times.

Sam R: Sending DM now. Also, I wasn’t sure whether commuter pre-tax requires an additional form — I selected it but don’t see a deduction line.

Miguel (Payroll): Commuter is usually active within one cycle but depends on vendor onboarding. If you chose to add monthly transit, we forward to the commuter provider and it shows as a pre-tax deduction on the next month if processed. I’ll check both HSA + commuter vendor feed.

Benefits Bot: Enrollment processed: ENR-2026-09-12-448. Status: confirmed -> queued for payroll.

Miguel (Payroll): Quick summary for visibility: Sam’s enrollment came in after the payroll cutoff (cutoff 11:00am PT). HSA will start next paycheck. Commuter upload to vendor missed today’s batch; I re-submitted, should reflect on next month statement.

Talia (People Ops): Sam, there’s no action needed on your side. For audit we like a screenshot of the benefits confirmation page. Can you drop one here or in #onboarding-assets?

Sam R: Dropped screenshot in #onboarding-assets. One more Q: if my first paycheck already had a premiums deduction and HSA didn’t, will the company prorate or adjust?

Miguel (Payroll): We don’t retroactively adjust benefits premiums unless there was an error. HSA is an employee pre-tax deferral separate from premium. Because premium was applied correctly and HSA missed, you won’t see a retroactive HSA deduction. We can, however, advise how to contribute the missed amount manually via payroll catch-up or personal transfer to your HSA outside payroll if you prefer. If you want a catch-up through payroll, I need written approval (reply here with: APPROVE PAYROLL CATCH-UP).

Priya L: Quick note from benefits: if you opt for catch-up in payroll we need to confirm contribution limits for the year. Priya (Benefits) can validate annual HSA limits before payroll does catch-up.

Sam R: APPROVE PAYROLL CATCH-UP — please proceed if possible. Also curious about whether holiday pay was pro-rated for partial month hires? I see prorated PTO on portal but not sure about holiday accrual.

Talia (People Ops): We prorate holiday pay for some contractors but for full-time employees holidays are normally company-wide and not prorated. If you were eligible on the holiday date, you'd receive it; partial-month hires that start after a holiday might not. Which holiday are you asking about?

Sam R: The company holiday on 2026-12-24 — I started 2026-12-01 so I assume eligible?

Talia (People Ops): Yes, you were on payroll before that date so you should get the holiday. I’ll confirm with payroll and post back.

Miguel (Payroll): Noted on catch-up approval. I’ll run the catch-up for one missed HSA contribution and add a one-time deduction next paycheck. Also confirmed holiday pay will be applied for 12/24.

Sam R: Thanks everyone! Appreciate the quick responses.

Talia (People Ops): Glad we could help — closing thread once adjustments post. :white_check_mark:
